reason_for_revision: Private tracking of omitted destinations used a shared atomic increment. This added contention to preparation even when callback work was cheap.
Per-source occurrence and group witnesses used unnecessary vertex-sized scalar storage.
A frozen source does not by itself prove an immutable weighted candidate when destination and graph-weight storage alias. The general proof required an additional runtime address-range guard.

changes: Chunk-local destination bitsets merged before owner execution, with no shared atomic increment during preparation.
A source-presence bitset and per-occurrence keep flags.
A fixed profitability floor with a force-on correctness control.
Explicit accumulator disjointness checks against graph headers, CSR rows, columns, weights and output storage.
A counterexample fixture in which a minimum update changes a later edge weight; the simplification must refuse this case.
